issues.quote: He meant it to strike the first minute of the new century.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about the repeater, its purpose, or any century. Its only time-related content is the 9, 10 and 11 o'clock readings and the 10:20 instruction.
issues.misreading: A solver could read this as a hint that the repeater's chime, or a specific midnight-type moment, matters to the timeline. It also suggests the time could be heard from the atelier by pressing the slide, a means of telling time that the sheet never gives.

issues.quote: I regulated my own watch myself, Inspector. I do not let anyone else's hand near it.
issues.fact: L1 records only that her watch was exact at nine o'clock. The sheet says nothing about whether it stayed exact afterwards, or about who has handled it.
issues.misreading: A solver could take this as confirmation that her watch kept true time through the night, including when she compared it in the kitchen. That would be a reliability claim the sheet does not make.
